items.title: The integral closure of a normal domain in a finite extension is reflexive
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the integral closure of a Noetherian normal domain in a finite field extension is reflexive as a module over the domain, assuming it is finite. The proof uses the criterion that a finite module over a normal domain is reflexive exactly when it is the intersection of its localisations at the height one primes. An element of that intersection is taken, its minimal polynomial over the fraction field is written down, and the cited result that the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of an integral element lie in the localisations at height one primes is applied; the intersection theorem for normal domains then puts those coefficients back into the domain, so the element was integral and lies in the integral closure.
